command: pre-registration of the two-stage family-transfer test

arms.control: the existing one-demo LoRA (m3_final tag lora; r3_fewshot.py): the same stage-2 call from a fresh adapter, so each arm is paired with it step for step
arms.r21fam: stage 1: LoRA on the family pool ALONE (the same pools as r20fam); stage 2: the one-demo LoRA's exact recipe from the stage-1 adapter
arms.r21rnd: the same with the size-matched random-task pool of r20rnd

metrics.experiment: two-stage family transfer: does a family's grammar transfer once the target's own binding is restored?
metrics.follows: m3_prereg tag family (NEGATIVE, reversed: pooling family data at training time made the adapter carry out a sibling's instruction)

hypotheses.T1: r21fam > the one-demo LoRA over the 12 targets (240 paired): exact two-sided sign test -- the family's pretraining helps once the binding is restored
hypotheses.T2: r21fam > r21rnd over the 12 targets (240 paired): exact two-sided sign test -- the help is family-specific (what the coarse levels would predict)
hypotheses.correction: T1 and T2 Holm-adjusted together; each passes at adjusted p < 0.05
hypotheses.secondary: the same within the pick-and-place family (140 pairs) and on the drawer family (60); r21rnd vs the one-demo LoRA

metrics.reading: T1 and T2 pass: the coarse levels predict transferable grammar once binding is separated -- value for the hierarchy; T1 passes, T2 fails: pretraining on any tasks helps, the families add nothing; both fail: cross-task sharing is closed in this setting (the fourth negative after the shared fold, the other half's fold and family pooling)
metrics.scoring: init states 30-49, 20 episodes per task and arm (m3_final tags lora_r21fam, lora_r21rnd)
metrics.training: stage 1: rank 16 on the action expert, 1000 steps, lr 1e-4, batch 32 uniform over the pool, seed 0; stage 2: every frame of the target's one demo, 1000 steps, lr 1e-4, batch 32, seed 0, fresh AdamW (experiments/r20_family.py --two-stage)
